event.text:
Execution plan:
- [step_1] Locate the placeholder interpolation implementation and the relevant tests. Identify placeholder syntax, expected replacement behavior, and how iteration boundaries are currently computed for adjacent and embedded placeholders. (investigation, mode: react, deps: none)
- [step_2] Reproduce the bug using existing tests or a minimal non-test command. Characterize failing cases involving adjacent placeholders and placeholders embedded within surrounding text. (investigation, mode: react, deps: step_1)
- [step_3] Determine the corrected boundary logic for scanning/replacing placeholders so that replacement consumes the entire placeholder and resumes at the correct position for adjacent and embedded cases. (design, mode: react, deps: step_2)
- [step_4] Modify only the repository source code implementing interpolation. Do not change tests, test files, or test/build configuration. (implementation, mode: react, deps: step_3)
- [step_5] Run the most relevant existing unittest(s) for interpolation to confirm adjacent and embedded placeholder behavior is fixed and no obvious regression was introduced. (verification, mode: react, deps: step_4)
- [step_6] From /workspace, run the acceptance command: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v. Confirm the full suite passes. (verification, mode: react, deps: step_5)

def resolve_variables(
    values: Iterable[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]],
    override: bool,
) -> Mapping[str, Optional[str]]:
    new_values: Dict[str, Optional[str]] = {}

    for name, value in values:
        if value is None:
            result = None
        else:
            atoms = parse_variables(value)
            env: Dict[str, Optional[str]] = {}
            if override:
                env.update(os.environ)  # type: ignore
                env.update(new_values)
            else:
                env.update(new_values)
                env.update(os.environ)  # type: ignore
            result = "".join(atom.resolve(env) for atom in atoms)

        new_values[name] = result

    return new_values
